clue.text: Taxonomic group originally unknown in southern confines

indicators.note: in places the letter taken from unknown inside the run of the other pieces

parts.note: the confines of a region are its border

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word unknown

explanation.surface: A biologist describes a classification group of species first found unidentified at the southern edge of their range.
explanation.definitionFit: A suborder is a rank in biological classification, sitting between order and family.

clue.text: Temporary building material on a Scottish island

parts.note: staff is a plaster mixture used for temporary buildings and exhibition work

explanation.surface: Makeshift construction materials have been shipped to an island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFA is a small Hebridean island, home of Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is an island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its basalt columns and Fingal's Cave.

clue.text: Drink with weaver, saying this in encouragement?

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A weaver at the bar urges his friends to drink up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links the pieces; the toast is said to encourage others to drain their glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a toast urging drinkers to empty their glasses, so it is said in encouragement.

clue.text: Oilman at home in advert

indicators.note: in places the at-home word inside the word for advert

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A petroleum worker relaxes at home during a commercial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advert' is not an advertisement but the verb: to advert to is to refer to.
explanation.definitionFit: A refiner processes crude oil, so he is an oilman in the trade sense.

clue.text: Edit notes about castles, for example

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two notes go around the chess pieces

parts.note: E and D are musical notes
castles (rooks) are chessmen, examples of men

explanation.surface: An editor jots notes about castles in the margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castles' are rooks on a chessboard, so pieces or MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and edit it.

clue.text: Posh fur fit to wear

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
sable is a luxurious fur

explanation.surface: A grand fur coat is declared good enough to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class (as in 'U and non-U' English) is a crossword staple for posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable can serve its purpose, as a garment in good condition can be worn.

clue.text: Novel hairstyle adopted for affair

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
a bang is a fringe of hair, the American term

explanation.surface: A new hairdo is taken up for a special occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an anagram signal or 'new'; it is the book SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang means an affair or business, as in 'the whole shebang'.

clue.text: Cry baronet recognised crossing meadow

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the baronet abbreviation spans the meadow word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow

explanation.surface: A baronet's shout is heard as he walks across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recognised' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleat is the cry of a sheep or goat.

clue.text: Attractive cake topping served by hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
icing tops a cake

explanation.surface: Tempting iced cakes are handed out by staff in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticing means tempting or attractive.

clue.text: Painstaking boss promises to pay

parts.note: a boss is a raised stud or knob
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A conscientious manager promises to settle debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager; it is a stud, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious can mean diligent and careful, painstaking in effort.

clue.text: Squaring-up process that made George I king?

definitions.meaning: a settling of accounts, the act of settling up a dispute or debt
the 1701 statute securing the Protestant succession, through which the Hanoverian George I gained the British throne

explanation.surface: A historian wonders what procedure of reckoning-up put the first George on the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1701 statute of that name fixed the succession on Sophia of Hanover's line, bringing George I to the throne in 1714.

clue.text: Accepting grant, little man looked worried

indicators.note: the little man's name takes in the word for grant, so it surrounds it

parts.note: Fred is a short man's name, the 'little' marking a diminutive form of Frederick
to grant a point is to own or admit it

explanation.surface: A small fellow, receiving a grant, looked anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like money being received; here it is the verb meaning admit, OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown is to wrinkle the brow, the look of someone worried or displeased.

clue.text: Desperate medic about to imbibe wine

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the doctor and the about-letter swallow the wine

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a medic
C stands for circa, Latin for about
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A doctor at the end of his tether is about to start drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to imbibe' reads as 'on the point of drinking'; in fact 'about' is C, and DR plus C take in ASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme ones, the sort taken when matters are desperate.

clue.text: Coffee from Home Counties retiring journalists love

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the abbreviation for the Home Counties is read backwards

parts.note: SE, the South East of England, is where the Home Counties around London lie
the press is journalists collectively
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Retired reporters in the Home Counties have a love of their morning coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Soldier — one who had a baton, say?

definitions.meaning: a non-commissioned army rank, a soldier above corporal

definitions.text: one who had a baton, say?
definitions.meaning: a police officer of that rank, who carries a baton or truncheon

explanation.surface: An army man recalls once carrying a marshal's baton.
explanation.walkthrough: The baton suggests a field marshal, but a police officer of the same title carries a truncheon.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank exists in both the army and the police, where officers carry batons.

clue.text: Banking system knight used for charge on shield

parts.note: a giro is a system of credit transfer between banks
N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A banking arrangement is used by a knight to pay for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee; in heraldry a charge is a figure on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a giron (gyron) is a triangular figure, one of the charges borne on a shield.

clue.text: Obscure woman's in preliminary survey involving husband

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the survey takes in the husband letter too
in places the woman's word inside the survey word

parts.note: a recce is a reconnaissance, a preliminary survey
her is the woman's possessive

explanation.surface: An obscure woman takes part in a first inspection that includes her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' and 'in' are two containers: the woman's word sits inside the survey, which then takes in the husband too. 'Obscure' looks like a verb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherche means rare or exotic, hence obscure or little known.

clue.text: Being transported from city stuck in a jam?

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
traffic stuck in a jam is static, not moving

explanation.surface: Commuters from the city are carried along, or stuck in a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being transported' looks like travel; it means carried away with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away with delight, utterly overjoyed.

clue.text: One who manages to buy and sell horses?

definitions.text: One who manages to buy and sell horses?

parts.words: One who manages to buy and sell horses?
parts.note: read one way, someone who copes; read another, an old word for a horse-dealer

explanation.definitionFit: A coper is a horse-dealer, and the word also suggests someone who copes or manages.

clue.text: Somehow use rise to get book brought out again

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A publisher uses a rise in demand to republish a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a new edition of a publication released again.

clue.text: Expedient to swap two characters in theology lectures

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject covering theology

indicators.note: exchanging a pair of letters rearranges the word for lectures

parts.note: a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: A divinity student considers it expedient to trade a pair of characters in their theology classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swap two characters in' switches the C and S of COURSE to give SOURCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A resource is a means or expedient one can turn to in difficulty.

clue.text: Like some notepaper without wrinkles?

definitions.meaning: plain paper, having no ruled guide-strokes on it
a face free of creases, not marked by age

explanation.definitionFit: Plain paper has no ruled lines, and a smooth face has no lines or wrinkles.

clue.text: Alarm shown when poisonous substance is mentione

indicators.note: mentioned (as the page's misspelling stands for) means spoken, so the word sounds like the poison

parts.note: a toxin is a poisonous substance

explanation.surface: A warning is sounded when someone mentions poison.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'mentione', a slip for 'mentioned', the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal.

clue.text: Italian word first used by English for white ant

indicators.note: first says the synonym for word comes before the Italian abbreviation

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A dictionary note says the Italian word for white ant was first adopted by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' just joins E onto the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are commonly called white ants, though they are not true ants.

clue.text: Think highly of lake creature with sweet tooth

parts.note: to rate someone is to think highly of them

explanation.surface: Someone admires a lakeside animal with a taste for sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: The RATEL is the honey badger, notorious for raiding bees' nests.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, raids beehives for honey, hence its sweet tooth.

clue.text: Remaining rejected, story's held to be outstanding work

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the story goes within the reversed word
rejected means turned back, so the word for remaining is read backwards

parts.note: over means remaining, as in food left over
a lie is a story, a fib; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A tale kept back for being left over turns out to be a remarkable piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' and 'held' work in turn: reverse first, then insert. 'outstanding' looks like praise but means standing out in relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo is relief sculpture, work that stands out from its background, hence outstanding.

clue.text: Country artist left to stalk game

indicators.note: to stalk is to follow behind, so the artist and left letters come after the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter in the countryside sets off to stalk game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is an adjective here, as in country life; 'game' is rugby, not quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means of the country rather than the town.

clue.text: Play Timothy's neighbour and cousin, oddly meeting resistance

parts.note: in the New Testament the epistle to Titus follows the two epistles to Timothy
taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: oddly signals that the word cousin is rearranged into a strange order

explanation.surface: A family drama: Timothy's neighbour and his cousin strangely meet with opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for odd letters but here signals an anagram: COUSIN becomes ONICUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Andronicus is an early Shakespeare tragedy.

clue.text: One visits everyone in church, regularly at first

indicators.note: in places the word for everyone inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
all means everyone

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of regularly

explanation.surface: A vicar calls on everyone in the church, regularly, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but 'at first' takes just its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller is a visitor, someone who calls at a house.

clue.text: Bachelor law lord has no say over club

parts.note: lud is lord, as in a barrister's 'm'lud' to a judge

indicators.note: over signals turning back, so the words no and say are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
eg (for example) is a way of saying 'say'

explanation.surface: An unmarried judge has no voice in the running of his club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns NO and EG together to make GEON; 'club' looks like a gentlemen's club but is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a short heavy club used as a weapon.
